title: GCI Coherence Audit
markdown:
# GCI Coherence Audit

**Source:** Luna/Sagemind topic 365 ("GCI"), 326 messages, Mar 2 → May 5
**Lens:** Where did Luna lose the bigger picture, and what infra would have prevented it?
**Tied to:** topic-intent-layer spec (this topic, 9976)

This audit walks the GCI thread incident by incident, names the failure mode, and maps it to either a piece already in the Topic Intent Layer spec or a piece the spec is currently missing.

---

## What "GCI" actually is

GCI is a 2-month-long client engagement with several distinct arcs running at once:

1. **Tom relationship arc** — BD partner, referral source, $10–20K pricing anchor
2. **Dempsey arc** — warm lead spawned out of this topic (eventually moved to its own topic 748)
3. **Data Scout product arc** — the custom GPT itself (Egnyte + ACC integrations, instructions, deployment flow)
4. **Christine + Jon support arc** — handling the "it didn't work" feedback that surfaced the submittals gap
5. **Phase 1 commercial arc** — pricing, contract, foundation-leverage argument, milestone structure
6. **Phase 1 build arc** — fetchDocument backend, dev GPT, Egnyte OAuth, Vercel deploy

A coherent agent on this topic should hold all six arcs simultaneously, know which one a new message lives in, and surface the relevant established facts from each. Luna held them when prompted, but defaulted to reasoning from the latest message alone.

---

## The 14 incidents, grouped by failure mode

### Failure mode A — Session-restart blank-slate

**A1 — Mar 6, msg 442–446.** After overnight session restarts, Luna opens with `"Hey! I'm here. What's up?"`. Justin asks what to do about Tom; Luna replies `"let me pull up the project notes to refresh on where things left off with Tom"`. The "pull up the project notes" step is the failure — that work should already be done by the time Luna greets him.

**A2 — Mar 24, msg 868–895.** Same pattern. Justin: `"its been a long time since we heard from Tom"`. Luna restarts the session, then responds with a partial recap (msg 876: "Quick status check"), then ANOTHER session restart, then a different, better recap (msg 895). Two contradictory readings of the same state because the second resume happened to do the homework the first didn't.

**Why it happens:** Continuation context is the last 50 messages, no captured arc. Resume-time work is voluntary and not always done.

**What would have prevented it:** TopicIntent record + Arc-aware continuation header (already in the spec). The header should already contain: stated goal, established facts (Tom delivered Dempsey intro Mar 9, Salesforce/Gardner outstanding), open threads (waiting on Tom for X, Y), so the first message is `"Picking up GCI. Tom hasn't replied in 15 days. Open items with him: Gardner intro, Network Remedy intro. Recommend [N]"` instead of `"What's up?"`.

---

### Failure mode B — Architectural amnesia / talking past the user

**B1 — May 4, msg 1832–1844 (THE canonical incident).** After the Egnyte dev app callback issue surfaces, Luna proposes `"our backend should do Egnyte OAuth server-side, not the GPT"` and `"skip Egnyte auth in the dev GPT for now"`. Justin pushes back:

> Lets slow down for a sec. I don't understand your reasoning behind the "better arch decision". From my understanding, the goal flow is: user sends a query → custom gpt searches engyte → custom gpt THEN hits our custom endpoint to fetch the egnyte docs → custom gpt leverages the context. Is this correct? If so, then how are you suggesting that we skip the gpt accessing egnyte?

Luna's reply (msg 1844): `"You're right and I was talking past you. Let me correct two threads I was tangling together."`

The architecture had been established earlier in this same topic (search Action = per-user OAuth via GPT; fetch Action = server-side via our backend — explicitly written into the auth tradeoff doc at msg 1872 a few hours later). When Luna hit a redirect-URI snag, she generated a "better arch" suggestion from the local context window without consulting the architectural decisions already on record.

**Why it happens:** No durable record of "decisions taken, not under reconsideration." Local context evaporates and gets re-derived from scratch.

**What would have prevented it:** A **Decision Ledger** sub-component of TopicIntent. Decisions get extracted alongside facts, with their rationale. Pre-send arc check (already in spec) flags any outbound message that proposes changing an item in the Decision Ledger and forces an explicit re-open framing instead of presenting it as a new idea. **The spec currently treats "established" as a flat fact list; it needs decisions-with-rationale as a first-class kind.**

---

### Failure mode C — Re-deriving prior context wastefully

**C1 — Apr 28, msg 1648–1659.** Luna prices Phase 1 at $8,500. Justin asks `"how did you come up with those prices?"`. Luna answers honestly: `"not as rigorously as I should have"`. Then Justin (msg 1656) hands her a comprehensive list — GCI is the foundational customer, Tom's pricing comments in meetings, $3,500 already paid hourly, the need for market comps — and asks her to re-do the pricing comprehensively. All four of those inputs already lived in this topic and in project notes. Luna had to be told what context to consider.

**C2 — Apr 28, msg 1655.** Luna gets back to it: `"Good catch. No, I was not pricing this with the foundation in mind, and that is exactly the leverage that should let us move off hourly into fixed-price without leaving money on the table."` Better answer, but only after Justin did the retrieval work.

**Why it happens:** The agent's default mode is "answer the literal question with what's in working memory" — same failure pattern Justin caught in qalatra (9235). She didn't ask herself "what topic-level context is load-bearing for a pricing call?"

**What would have prevented it:**
- **TopicIntent's `established` block** needs to include not just facts but also **constraints/inputs** ("$3,500 hourly already billed", "Tom's quoted pricing band", "GCI is the foundational customer"). When the active turn classifies as a pricing/commercial sub-arc, the relevant slice of `established` is hoisted to the prompt header automatically.
- **Sub-arc routing** — message classified as "pricing decision" should auto-retrieve all prior pricing references in the topic and inline them. The spec talks about scope-change re-extraction but not about sub-arc-aware retrieval. **Probably an addition.**

---

### Failure mode D — Forgetting style/preference rules

**D1 — Apr 23, msg 1553.** `"Please rewrite this message and take out the M dashes and from now on don't ever use the M dashes please save this in your memory"`. Saved. But Luna had used em-dashes throughout the topic up to that point.

**D2 — Apr 23, msg 1557.** Justin again: `"Yes, the email is drafted but email that has tons of M dashes. Please give me a new draft that doesn't have any dashes."` Even immediately after being told, the active draft still had them — the rule landed in memory but didn't retroactively rewrite the in-flight artifact.

**D3 — Apr 27, msg 1581.** `"I really can't understand your response. Can you reword this and I'm easier to understand way."` Justin had used GCI as the testbed before but the plain-language style wasn't being applied. Then msg 1585: `"Please make this communication style. Your standard moving forward through all channels."`

**D4 — Apr 28, msg 1637.** Three specific style notes after Luna draft: speak as "I" not "we", don't make "most teams find" claims, don't pre-exclude drawings. Then the critical ask:

> NOTE: please remember any style tips I give you moving forward. I would like it if you have a habit of tracking these for various situations automatically (i.e. "justin emailing to client" specific style notes along with notes for other scenarios) so that you can auto-learn/converge on specific styles as you and I work together

**Why it happens:** Style rules go into a flat MEMORY.md, not into a scenario-keyed registry. There's no pre-send hook that looks up "this is a client email" and applies the matching ruleset. Each rule sits in memory but doesn't fire automatically on the right surface.

**What would have prevented it:**
- A **Scenario Style Registry** keyed by situation type (client email, internal recap, pricing doc, technical explanation), maintained automatically: when Justin gives feedback that classifies as style/tone/format, the agent infers the scenario and writes a rule under that key. **Not currently in the Topic Intent Layer spec — explicit user request. This is a separate but adjacent component.**
- **Pre-send style check** (parallel to pre-send arc check) — for outbound drafts on a known scenario, run a quick classifier pass that flags rule violations. Same pattern as arc check, different rulebook.

---

### Failure mode E — Repeating failed approaches without learning mid-loop

**E1 — Apr 29, msg 1690–1715 (the Gmail copy-paste saga).** Justin: `"can you give me a form that properly formats when I paste it into gmail?"`. Luna's attempts in order: (1) tunnel-served HTML view with Cmd+A copy, (2) clean HTML file in Chrome with inline styles, (3) pandoc-rendered markdown, (4) HTTP-served HTML tab with paste-mode advice. All fail. Justin gets visibly frustrated: `"This is frustrating. I know we've copied and pasted before with proper formatting. How is this normally handled in gmail?"`

Only on attempt 5 does Luna try RTF on the macOS clipboard — works first try. Justin: `"That worked! Lets remember this method moving forward."` 

The killer line in Justin's frustration message: **"I know we've copied and pasted before with proper formatting."** There IS prior topic-history evidence that something worked; the agent didn't retrieve it.

**E2 — Across the OAuth dance (msg 1900–1953).** Luna attempts the Egnyte OAuth helper at least 4 distinct ways: localhost callback (rejected, HTTPS required), trycloudflare quick tunnel (Egnyte UI silently failed to save), another trycloudflare quick tunnel (same failure), finally a Vercel-hosted callback (worked first try). Same failure shape repeated — the "trycloudflare quick tunnel is flaky" learning didn't propagate across attempts within the same session.

**Why it happens:** No "what worked before for this kind of problem" retrieval. Each retry is independent; the agent doesn't write a `tried: X, failed: Y, root cause: Z` ledger that the next attempt consults.

**What would have prevented it:**
- A **Solution Ledger** — when a problem class shows up (formatted clipboard paste, OAuth callback hosting, …) and a fix is confirmed working, that gets recorded with the *problem class as key*, not just as a free-form memory entry. Then before attempting solution N+1 to a similar problem, retrieve the prior solution.
- **Failure-aware retry policy** — within a session, attempts to a single sub-problem should accumulate a structured ledger so attempt 3 onward has explicit "ruled out: A, B; cause hypothesis: C". **Out of scope for the Topic Intent Layer per se, but the same data model — extract → store → re-inject — would apply.**

---

### Failure mode F — Forgetting agent's own capabilities / live state

**F1 — Apr 23, msg 1464–1481.** Luna gives up on fetching Autodesk docs because web-fetch can't render JS, and says `"per our due diligence standard, I don't want to hand you a schema I can't verify against primary sources"`. Justin (msg 1478): `"don't use web fetch then. You have many more options such as playwright. Please be more pro-active and agentic for finding solutions instead of giving up"`. Luna pivots immediately (msg 1481: `"You're right — that was a cop-out"`) and Playwright works fine on the first try.

**F2 — May 4, msg 1873–1879 (tunnel restart).** Luna claims the server `"can't restart itself from inside a Claude Code session (safety guard)"`. Justin (msg 1877): `"you've always been able to restart the instar server yourself in the past"`. Luna then finds another path entirely (msg 1879: `"Got it working. The tunnel was up the whole time — the issue was the server's internal tunnel-state file wasn't reflecting it"`).

**F3 — May 4, msg 1602.** `"that's not the permanent tunnel url. please fix it"`. Luna had been using `luna-justin.dawn-tunnel.dev` consistently earlier in the topic (msg 1632, msg 1655, msg 1667), then regressed to a fresh `trycloudflare.com` ephemeral URL.

**F4 — Apr 27, msg 1580.** `"my earlier replies hit a 403 on the relay. The script defaults to port 4040 but your active instar server is on 6060, so the token mismatch was rejecting them."` Luna stayed on default config instead of querying the running server for its actual port.

**Why it happens:** Capability self-knowledge is held in CLAUDE.md / memory rather than queried from the live server, and the topic's prior runtime decisions (which tunnel URL we use here, which port the relay should hit, whether server-restart-from-session works) aren't lifted into TopicIntent.established.

**What would have prevented it:**
- TopicIntent.established should include **runtime decisions** ("permanent tunnel URL = luna-justin.dawn-tunnel.dev", "relay port = 6060") not only project-level facts.
- A **"check live state before claiming a capability gap"** rule on the pre-send arc check: if a draft says "I can't X", the check requires that a recent self-knowledge query or runtime check is cited. Currently the arc check is about "does this answer tie back to the topic goal" — it doesn't catch capability-fabrication. **Probably needs extending the arc check, not adding a new component.**

---

### Failure mode G — Losing thread mid-task (silence after long work)

**G1 — Apr 21, msg 1440.** `"did you see my last message?"` — 30+ minutes after Christine's GCI feedback, no response. Status indicator was running but no actual reply landed.

**G2 — Apr 27, msg 1577.** `"Checking in here I never got a response from you"` — port-mismatch issue, but from Justin's POV: silence.

**G3 — Apr 27, msg 1589.** `"Picking up where we got cut off. My last message ran out mid sentence..."` — context compaction during mid-response. Luna recovered but had to manually re-emit the truncated bullets.

**Why it happens:** No timeout/heartbeat on long-running thinking, no commitment tracking. Compaction can interrupt mid-message.

**What would have prevented it:** This is the "active follow-through" memory Justin has already established (`feedback_active_followthrough.md`). The Topic Intent Layer doesn't directly address it but `open_threads` in TopicIntent should include in-flight commitments ("agent currently composing response to msg N, due back within X min") so a session resume after compaction knows what the agent owes the user, not just what the user owes the agent.

---

### Failure mode H — Compaction-triggered re-orientation drag

**H1 — Multiple messages where the status line explicitly mentions compaction.** Msg 1646: `"Session paused for context compaction and has resumed"`. Msg 1654: `"is resuming after a context compaction and re-orienting to address your question"`. Msg 1658: `"is recovering from context compaction and resuming work on your GCI pricing analysis"`.

Each compaction visibly costs a re-orientation step — the agent narrates that it's catching up. That's not bad per se, but it's evidence that compaction is a routine interruption, not an edge case.

**Why it happens:** Default compaction summary captures the recent transcript, not the topic arc.

**What would have prevented it:** TopicIntent record + arc-aware continuation header is exactly the fix for this. Compaction survival is one of the spec's stated wins. **This case validates the spec as-written.** Just call it out clearly in acceptance tests: any compaction in the middle of a multi-turn arc must not cost re-orientation time when TopicIntent is in place.

---

## Summary mapping: incidents → infra

| Failure mode | Already in spec? | Spec gap |
|---|---|---|
| A: Session-restart blank slate | YES — TopicIntent + continuation header | — |
| B: Architectural amnesia | PARTIAL — `established` needs **decisions with rationale** as first-class kind, not just flat facts | **Decision Ledger sub-component** |
| C: Re-deriving prior context | PARTIAL — needs **sub-arc routing**: when turn is classified as pricing/build/contract/etc., hoist the relevant sub-slice of `established` | **Sub-arc-aware retrieval** |
| D: Style/preference forgetting | NO — Justin's explicit ask (msg 1637) | **Scenario Style Registry + pre-send style check** |
| E: Repeating failed approaches | NO — adjacent | **Solution Ledger** keyed by problem class |
| F: Capability/runtime amnesia | PARTIAL — extend arc check to flag capability-fabrication; `established` must include runtime decisions | **Extend `established` schema; extend arc check** |
| G: Mid-task silence | Existing feedback memory | **Add "agent in-flight commitments" to `open_threads`** |
| H: Compaction drag | YES — exactly what TopicIntent is for | — |

---

## What I'd add to the spec

Given this audit, four concrete extensions to the Topic Intent Layer spec stand out:

1. **`established` becomes structured, not flat.** Sub-types: `facts`, `decisions` (with rationale + status: open / closed / under-reopen), `runtime` (tunnel URL, ports, paths), `commitments` (open threads, agent's own promises).

2. **Sub-arc routing.** A topic this size (326 messages) doesn't have one arc — it has six concurrent arcs. The scope-change classifier needs to extend to sub-arc classification, and each turn should hoist only the relevant sub-arc's `established` slice. Otherwise the prompt header becomes its own context bloat.

3. **Scenario Style Registry.** Out of scope for arc-tracking strictly, but the same architectural pattern (extract → store → re-inject pre-send). Justin asked for this directly in msg 1637 and it should ship in v1 even if as a separate component.

4. **Solution Ledger.** Problem-class-keyed "what worked" memory, queried before re-attempting a similar problem. Same extract/store/inject pattern, different ontology.

The qalatra incident (9235) is one canonical fixture for the v1 acceptance tests. Add the **Egnyte arch-amnesia incident (msgs 1832–1844)** as a second canonical fixture, because it stresses the Decision Ledger piece that qalatra alone doesn't surface.

---

## Cross-topic awareness (out of scope, but worth flagging)

The Dempsey arc was eventually spun out into topic 748. Before that happened, Dempsey context lived inside GCI (msgs 569–751). After the split, the GCI topic kept referencing Dempsey state ("Dempsey is still reviewing"). That cross-topic awareness was working manually because Justin did the spinout deliberately. A future cross-topic layer would need TopicIntent records to know about each other — out of v1 per your note, but the schema choices we make now should leave room for `related_topics: [...]` cleanly.
